subject: Production-mode recommendation and throughput limits — OptiRetail pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@opti-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Production-mode recommendation and throughput limits — OptiRetail pilot

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed path so we can converge on a pilot config: 

Recap (what we heard)
- OptiRetail wants a real-time recommendation API for checkout suggestions.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~60–80 QPS during normal business hours, with peak spikes up to ~200 QPS for flash events.
- Typical request payload: ~1.6 KB (customer data + item context).
- Must keep 95th percentile latency under ~150ms for the checkout flow; p99 target is 300ms but you prefer to hit p99 < 200ms if possible.
- Security: SC-1 compliance checklist required; public cloud is acceptable but you may want VPC peering for production later.

Our recommendation (short)
- Pilot: Dedicated reserved capacity (small pool) for predictable tail-latency and stable throughput. We propose reserve capacity sized for sustained 100–150 QPS with headroom to 250 QPS for bursts. This keeps p95 low and makes tuning easier.
- Fallback: Enable Hosted API spillover for infrequent bursts above reserved capacity (technical details below).
- Private/VPC: Recommended only if your security team requires strict network controls or on-prem for regulated data; we can scope later.

Immediate asks for sizing & SOW
1) Can you confirm expected median and 95th percentile request size and a rough distribution across hours? (I attached a simple CSV template: pilot-benchmark-ask.csv)
2) Do you expect any synchronous third-party calls inside the critical path (yes/no)?
3) Are you comfortable starting on Dedicated for 4 weeks with hosted fallback enabled?

What we'll do once you confirm
- Ben will propose a starter config (GPU type, # replicas, batching window) and an estimated cost range.
- Monica will draft a short SOW and pilot timeline.
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff with CS + infra to align telemetry and SLOs.

Attachments: pilot-benchmark-ask.csv (please fill in traffic samples if you can)

Thanks — aim to get the kickoff on the calendar this week if possible.

— Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifying Qs.

Answers:
- Payload: median ~1.5 KB, p95 ~2.3 KB. I filled the CSV with a rough hour-by-hour sample and uploaded to the link you shared.
- Third-party calls: we have an enrichment call to inventory that is currently synchronous for ~30% of requests; we can work to make that async but not before the pilot.
- Dedicated pilot: we’re okay trying Dedicated + hosted fallback for burst handling.

Clarifying Qs:
- When you say "headroom to 250 QPS," is that per instance group or total cluster? We typically see simultaneous spikes across multiple storefronts in the same minute.
- Can Redwood’s hosted fallback ensure request affinity so we don’t lose session-level context?

Also looping in Carlos (ops) who will be the main point for security/compliance — he is on this thread.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Production-mode recommendation and throughput limits — OptiRetail pilot

Alex / Hannah — quick technical note after looking at the numbers Alex dropped into the CSV. Quoting the relevant bit from Alex: 

> Payload: median ~1.5 KB, p95 ~2.3 KB. Third-party inventory call synchronous ~30% of requests.

Recommendation & rationale:
- Dedicated sizing: start with 2x A10G-equivalent instances (reserved) behind our inference pool manager with autoscaling rules that prefer vertical scaling within the pool up to that headroom. That configuration should handle sustained ~120–150 QPS with p95 < 140ms for your median payload.
- Burst plan: configure hosted fallback as a secondary route. Requests will flow to the fallback when queue depth exceeds thresholds; we retain session metadata via our signed KV cookie and replicated small-context cache so affinity is preserved for short windows (we’ll document limits in the SOW).
- Inventory call: that synchronous dependency will drive tail variance. Two mitigations: (1) implement a short timeout and partial-response strategy in the pilot; (2) add a small per-request cache layer at Redwood edge for inventory lookups if the keys are cacheable.

Pilot config artifacts: I attached a starter pilot-config.yaml (conceptual) with batching window = 8ms, max tokens per request = 512, and prewarm concurrency = 2 per replica. We’ll refine after we get production-like traces.

Rough cost guideline (very rough): Dedicated reserved pool (2x A10G eq) ~ $XXk/month committed — we’ll provide a formal number in the SOW. Hosted fallback billed per-token on overflow.

If that aligns, I can convert this into an engineering runbook and checklist for the kickoff.

— Ben

Alex / team — thanks for the quick turn. This is helpful. Action items and proposed dates below so we can lock the pilot in: 

Action items (who / when)
1) Alex / OptiRetail: confirm hour-by-hour CSV and call dependency list (inventory is marked). Please paste any production traces you can share by EOD Thu Nov 5. (Alex)
2) Ben: prepare a short runbook + initial cost ranges and post the pilot-config.yaml into the Drive folder. Deliver by Fri Nov 6. (Ben)
3) Monica: draft a 4-week SOW with pilot acceptance criteria and hosted-fallback terms; include a basic data-handling addendum for the inventory enrichment scenario. Deliver initial draft by Mon Nov 9. (Monica)
4) Schedule: propose kickoff Wed Nov 11 at 10am PT — 30 minutes (CS, infra, OptiRetail eng). If that works Alex, I’ll send the invite.

Decision summary for the pilot (written)
- Mode: Dedicated reserved pool sized for sustained 120–150 QPS with hosted overflow enabled.
- Goal: hit p95 < 150ms, p99 < 250ms for the checkout recommendation path.
- Duration: 4 weeks with acceptance criteria tied to latency and correctness on a set of test prompts.

Attachments referenced: pilot-benchmark-ask.csv (uploaded), pilot-config.yaml (Ben will drop a version), initial SOW draft (Monica will prepare) — I’ve attached a placeholder SOW-draft-opti-rotating.pdf for contract team context.

Please reply with any objections to the plan; otherwise I’ll schedule kickoff and loop in CS.

— Hannah
